hero.headline: Martin County deputies save senior from $600,000 gold bar scam
hero.teaser: A Martin County senior citizen nearly lost $600,000 to a scam in which a fraudster posed as a bank representative and convinced the victim to buy gold bars, but deputies intervened to stop the transaction.
hero.body:
A Martin County senior citizen nearly lost $600,000 to a gold bar scam, but deputies helped avert the loss. The Martin County Sheriff's Office said the victim was contacted by a fraudster claiming to be from his financial institution and was told that his bank account had been compromised. The scammer then convinced the senior citizen that he needed to protect his money by backing it up with gold.

According to the sheriff's office, the victim was instructed to send $600,000 to a legitimate gold vendor. The scammer told the victim that the gold would then be picked up by a third-party driver and delivered to the bank. After going through with the transaction, the victim quickly realized something was wrong and immediately went to his bank. The bank recognized the situation as potential fraud and advised him to contact the sheriff's office.

The responding deputy spoke directly with the gold vendor and helped the victim stop the transaction from going through. The sheriff's office said the victim confirmed he received a full refund of his $600,000.

cards.headline: More Than 70 Animals Found in Stuart Home During Large-Scale Hoarding Response
cards.teaser: 77-year-old Gail Giustino was arrested on two misdemeanor animal cruelty-related charges following the search of a Stuart home where Martin County authorities found more than 70 an
cards.body:
The Martin County Building Department condemned a Palm City home on Wednesday after authorities arrested Paige O'Donnell on 72 charges in connection with hoarding 36 Border Collies in what the Humane Society of the Treasure Coast called the worst animal hoarding case in its history. The notice posted to the gate states occupancy is prohibited as the structure is unfit for human occupancy under section 21.75.3, citing an unsanitary single-family residence.

The Martin County Sheriff's Office arrested O'Donnell on Monday following a lengthy investigation into animal welfare concerns at her residence. When deputies executed a search warrant, they discovered dogs covered in feces and urine living in a home with no functioning air conditioning and floors covered in waste and garbage, according to a probable cause affidavit. Deputies noted the condition of the dogs and surrounding environment was such that the animals were difficult to distinguish from the heavily soiled areas of the residence.

Animal Control Officer Tabitha Queen documented approximately 20 related incidents at the address spanning from 2020 through 2026. During an August 3 meeting at Jock Leighton Park in Palm City, O'Donnell told the officer she owned only four dogs, but records from Boulevard Animal Hospital identified approximately 38 adult dogs associated with O'Donnell. The clinic employee said there were so many puppies brought in with O'Donnell that it was impossible to get an accurate count, with the last recorded visit on June 25, 2022.

O'Donnell faces 72 total charges, including 36 counts of felony animal cruelty and 36 misdemeanor counts for failing to provide the dogs with proper exercise or air. A judge set her total bond at $275,000 and ordered that she may not own or possess any animals as a condition of her bond. The Humane Society of the Treasure Coast is providing urgent care for the 36 Border Collies, including three puppies up to six months old, with staff working around the clock to medically groom, bathe and examine the dogs.

cards.headline: Vehicle connected to fatal hit-and-run in Indian River County recovered
cards.teaser: The Indian River County Sheriff's Office announced Wednesday that a vehicle connected to a deadly hit-and-run crash on Sunday has been recovered.
cards.body:
The Indian River County Sheriff's Office announced Wednesday that a vehicle connected to a deadly hit-and-run crash on Sunday, Aug. 9, has been recovered. The sheriff's office said its Real-Time Crime Center assisted the Florida Highway Patrol in the investigation, which led to the discovery.

A vehicle matching the description of the suspected truck was identified by the Real-Time Crime Center analyst. The truck was missing a passenger-side mirror. Using other technology, the analyst identified the truck's license plate and associated driver information. The information was immediately given to FHP, which located the truck and confirmed it was involved in the crash with a bicyclist.

The investigation continues in identifying the driver of the truck.

cards.headline: Indian River County deputies talk wanted man off 17th Street Bridge after two-hour standoff
cards.teaser: Indian River County sheriff's deputies successfully ended a two-hour standoff on the 17th Street Bridge in Vero Beach after talking a man wanted for burglary back from the edge. De
cards.body:
Indian River County deputies safely took a man into custody after a two-hour standoff on the 17th Street Bridge early Tuesday morning. The incident began around 1 a.m. when deputies responded to a call from Port St. Lucie police about a man wanted for burglary who had called his mother and told her he wanted to kill himself.

Body camera footage showed the man sitting on a platform over the bridge railing with his feet dangling in the air. Traffic Deputy Edouard Gast, a member of the Indian River County Sheriff's Office Crisis Negotiation Team, worked to establish a connection with the man. Gast said the man at first did not want to talk, and it took time to get him to open up. At one point, the man appeared ready to jump. Gast continued to plead with him, saying, "Come on, man, don't do this to your mom."

Gast said the man flipped a switch and climbed on top, positioning himself to jump. Gast talked to him repeatedly until the man climbed back over and stood on the platform. The sheriff's office marine unit and fire rescue crews were stationed in the water below as a safety precaution.

After two hours of negotiation, the man climbed back to the top of the bridge and shook the negotiator's hand. The man was taken into custody without incident. Sgt. from the sheriff's office said that even though the man was wanted out of Port St. Lucie, deputies still treated him with due care to make sure he was safe and could answer for his crimes.

cards.headline: Mets, Tortugas split Saturday doubleheader as Zayas powers Game 1 win
cards.teaser: Julio Zayas hit a go-ahead three-run homer for the second straight day, lifting St. Lucie to a 3-1 win before Daytona answered with a 15-7 victory in Game 2.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets and Daytona Tortugas split a Saturday doubleheader at Clover Park, with the Mets taking the opener 3-1 before Daytona answered with a 15-7 victory in Game 2.

The split left the seven-game series tied 3-3 heading into Sunday’s finale. It was also the second time the teams split a doubleheader during the series after each club won once during Wednesday’s twin bill.

## Zayas delivers another go-ahead home run

Julio Zayas provided the biggest swing for St. Lucie in Game 1, hitting a go-ahead three-run home run in the fourth inning to erase a 1-0 Daytona lead.

The homer came one night after Zayas hit a walk-off home run in the bottom of the ninth inning Friday. Saturday’s blast was his third home run of the series.

St. Lucie’s pitching staff made the lead hold up.

Starter Nate Hall worked the first 1 2/3 innings before Caden Wooster took over. Wooster allowed Daytona’s only run when Arnaldo Lantigua hit a solo home run in the third inning.

Ernesto Mercedes followed with two scoreless innings, allowing four hits while striking out three to earn the win.

Miguel Mijias recorded the final five outs for his fourth save of the season, including a perfect seventh inning to close the game.

The Mets held Daytona to 1-for-8 with runners in scoring position and stranded 10 Tortugas runners.

The performance continued a sharp turnaround for St. Lucie’s pitching staff. From the ninth inning of Thursday’s game through the end of Saturday’s opener, the Mets allowed only one run after Daytona had scored 17 runs over the first eight innings Thursday.

Daytona starter Dusty Revis was charged with the loss despite throwing a six-inning complete game on just 63 pitches. Revis allowed five hits and three earned runs while becoming the first Tortugas pitcher since 2019 to record a complete game.

Elian Peña went 1-for-3 for St. Lucie and extended his hitting streak to 10 games.

## Daytona pulls away in Game 2

The nightcap was a much different game, with Daytona breaking a 6-6 tie during a decisive fifth inning.

Mets newcomer Wilmer Lugo appeared to escape the inning by striking out Henry Hunter looking on a 3-2 pitch. Hunter challenged the call using the ABS system, however, and the ruling was overturned to ball four, loading the bases.

Lugo then walked the next two hitters to force home a pair of runs. After Luis Sotillo entered in relief, a wild pitch allowed Hunter to score and stretched Daytona’s lead to 9-6.

Hunter delivered another major blow in the seventh inning, hitting a grand slam off Sotillo to push the Tortugas ahead 13-6.

For the second time in four games, the Mets eventually turned to Zayas to finish the game on the mound as a position player. He recorded the final four outs, allowing a two-run homer to Drew Davies with two outs in the seventh but no additional damage.

Logan Tanner earned the win for Daytona after throwing two scoreless innings of relief.

St. Lucie still produced several offensive highlights in the loss.

Simon Juan went 2-for-3 with a double and his ninth home run of the season.

Kuhio Aloy, the Mets’ 11th-round draft pick, hit a two-run homer in the third inning to tie the game at 6-6. It was Aloy’s first professional home run.

Lugo took the loss after being charged with three runs on one hit and four walks over 2/3 of an inning.

## Series finale set for Sunday

The Mets fell to 16-24 in the second half and 49-57 overall, while Daytona improved to 25-14 in the second half and 46-60 overall.

St. Lucie and Daytona will decide the series Sunday at Clover Park, with first pitch scheduled for 12:10 p.m.

Sunday is Little League Day. Little leaguers who attend wearing their team jerseys will receive free admission courtesy of Holiday Inn Express.

cards.headline: Trail camera, AirTags fuel sign theft allegations between Martin County candidates
cards.teaser: A Martin County Commission candidate says he caught a campaign sign thief on a trail camera and tracked stolen signs with AirTags, igniting a public clash between political candidates in the final days before the August election.
cards.body:
Chris Collins, running for Martin County Commission Seat Two, posted a video to Facebook claiming he caught a man stealing his campaign signs using a hunting trail camera. In the video, Collins stands in front of a still photo showing a man in a darkened area at night holding one of his campaign signs. Collins, formerly the Mayor of Stuart, said he set up the trail cam after some of his signs went missing and put Apple AirTags on some of the signs to track their location.

Collins identified the man as Jim Gallegos and said the signs were tracked to Gallegos' house. Collins claimed Gallegos is a campaign advisor to Merritt Matheson, another political candidate, though not in the same race as Collins. Gallegos denied the accusation, saying he was taking down signs that the property owner had requested be removed. Merritt Matheson sent a text saying Gallegos is not his campaign advisor.

The story of the stolen signs prompted Derreck Ogden, who is running for election to be a Stuart City Commissioner, to confront Gallegos. Their argument about the campaign signs was caught on camera and posted on Facebook. Gallegos said he removed about 30 campaign signs for various candidates, not just Chris Collins' campaign, because the property owner did not want the signs on his property. Gallegos said he no longer has the campaign signs.

hero.teaser: A Martin County senior citizen nearly lost $600,000 to a scam in which a fraudster posed as a bank representative and convinced the victim to buy gold bars, but deputies intervened to stop the transaction.
hero.body:
A Martin County senior citizen nearly lost $600,000 to a gold bar scam, but deputies helped avert the loss. The Martin County Sheriff's Office said the victim was contacted by a fraudster claiming to be from his financial institution and was told that his bank account had been compromised. The scammer then convinced the senior citizen that he needed to protect his money by backing it up with gold.

According to the sheriff's office, the victim was instructed to send $600,000 to a legitimate gold vendor. The scammer told the victim that the gold would then be picked up by a third-party driver and delivered to the bank. After going through with the transaction, the victim quickly realized something was wrong and immediately went to his bank. The bank recognized the situation as potential fraud and advised him to contact the sheriff's office.

The responding deputy spoke directly with the gold vendor and helped the victim stop the transaction from going through. The sheriff's office said the victim confirmed he received a full refund of his $600,000.

cards.headline: Trail camera, AirTags fuel sign theft allegations between Martin County candidates
cards.teaser: A Martin County Commission candidate says he caught a campaign sign thief on a trail camera and tracked stolen signs with AirTags, igniting a public clash between political candidates in the final days before the August election.
cards.body:
Chris Collins, running for Martin County Commission Seat Two, posted a video to Facebook claiming he caught a man stealing his campaign signs using a hunting trail camera. In the video, Collins stands in front of a still photo showing a man in a darkened area at night holding one of his campaign signs. Collins, formerly the Mayor of Stuart, said he set up the trail cam after some of his signs went missing and put Apple AirTags on some of the signs to track their location.

Collins identified the man as Jim Gallegos and said the signs were tracked to Gallegos' house. Collins claimed Gallegos is a campaign advisor to Merritt Matheson, another political candidate, though not in the same race as Collins. Gallegos denied the accusation, saying he was taking down signs that the property owner had requested be removed. Merritt Matheson sent a text saying Gallegos is not his campaign advisor.

The story of the stolen signs prompted Derreck Ogden, who is running for election to be a Stuart City Commissioner, to confront Gallegos. Their argument about the campaign signs was caught on camera and posted on Facebook. Gallegos said he removed about 30 campaign signs for various candidates, not just Chris Collins' campaign, because the property owner did not want the signs on his property. Gallegos said he no longer has the campaign signs.

hero.headline: Indian River County deputies talk wanted man off 17th Street Bridge after two-hour standoff
hero.teaser: Indian River County sheriff's deputies successfully ended a two-hour standoff on the 17th Street Bridge in Vero Beach after talking a man wanted for burglary back from the edge. De
hero.body:
Indian River County deputies safely took a man into custody after a two-hour standoff on the 17th Street Bridge early Tuesday morning. The incident began around 1 a.m. when deputies responded to a call from Port St. Lucie police about a man wanted for burglary who had called his mother and told her he wanted to kill himself.

Body camera footage showed the man sitting on a platform over the bridge railing with his feet dangling in the air. Traffic Deputy Edouard Gast, a member of the Indian River County Sheriff's Office Crisis Negotiation Team, worked to establish a connection with the man. Gast said the man at first did not want to talk, and it took time to get him to open up. At one point, the man appeared ready to jump. Gast continued to plead with him, saying, "Come on, man, don't do this to your mom."

Gast said the man flipped a switch and climbed on top, positioning himself to jump. Gast talked to him repeatedly until the man climbed back over and stood on the platform. The sheriff's office marine unit and fire rescue crews were stationed in the water below as a safety precaution.

After two hours of negotiation, the man climbed back to the top of the bridge and shook the negotiator's hand. The man was taken into custody without incident. Sgt. from the sheriff's office said that even though the man was wanted out of Port St. Lucie, deputies still treated him with due care to make sure he was safe and could answer for his crimes.

cards.headline: Vehicle connected to fatal hit-and-run in Indian River County recovered
cards.teaser: The Indian River County Sheriff's Office announced Wednesday that a vehicle connected to a deadly hit-and-run crash on Sunday has been recovered.
cards.body:
The Indian River County Sheriff's Office announced Wednesday that a vehicle connected to a deadly hit-and-run crash on Sunday, Aug. 9, has been recovered. The sheriff's office said its Real-Time Crime Center assisted the Florida Highway Patrol in the investigation, which led to the discovery.

A vehicle matching the description of the suspected truck was identified by the Real-Time Crime Center analyst. The truck was missing a passenger-side mirror. Using other technology, the analyst identified the truck's license plate and associated driver information. The information was immediately given to FHP, which located the truck and confirmed it was involved in the crash with a bicyclist.

The investigation continues in identifying the driver of the truck.
